repositories.name: AURORA
repositories.title: AURORA
repositories.description: A hackathon prototype that correlates cyber, physical, and intelligence events into evidence-linked alerts. A Python graph pipeline combines timing, location, semantic similarity, and shared entities; a React dashboard exposes the results, with optional AI analyst and voice integrations for incident review.

repositories.name: Watchpost
repositories.title: Watchpost
repositories.description: A native Apple-platform incident-triage app that keeps incident analysis on the device. Local text similarity finds related incidents, deterministic rules rank priority, and optional Apple Foundation Models generate briefs. Siri, Shortcuts, and Spotlight connect incident logging, triage, and resolution to everyday workflows.

repositories.name: QA-testbot
repositories.title: Patchsentry review engine
repositories.description: A pull-request QA engine that treats proposed code as untrusted input. Trusted runners execute tests in restricted containers, bind evidence and human decisions to an exact commit, and keep optional AI analysis separate from deterministic results. Browser checks and local model policies add explicit execution boundaries.

repositories.name: patchsentry-web
repositories.title: Patchsentry workspace
repositories.description: The account and reporting layer for Patchsentry, built with owner-scoped data access, secure sessions, login rate limits and hashed runner tokens. An outbound connector submits bounded reports and executes jobs only within a locally enrolled policy, keeping product-code execution outside the public web server.

repositories.name: WARBREAK
repositories.title: WARBREAK / FOGLINE
repositories.description: An exercise-planning prototype that extracts assumptions from a written plan, scores their fragility with an explicit rubric, and traces dependencies through a turn-based simulation. A local evidence catalog, fallback extraction, and post-exercise analysis support exploration of risk, resilience, and failure chains.

repositories.name: devflow-ai
repositories.title: DevFlow AI
repositories.description: A Python prototype exploring security review within an AI-assisted development pipeline. It generates code and test files, asks Claude to identify vulnerabilities, attempts remediation, rescans the result and opens a GitLab merge request with risk context. The dashboard streams workflow events and records run history.

repositories.name: Automated-Server-Provisioning-with-Ansible
repositories.title: Server provisioning with Ansible
repositories.description: Ansible configuration for Linux web and database servers, with package installation, admin-user setup, and Nginx and MariaDB service tasks. A learning lab that connects repeatable provisioning with explicit service configuration.

repositories.name: rclone-Amazon-S3-project
repositories.title: File transfers to Amazon S3
repositories.description: A shell-script lab for copying files from a Linux virtual machine to Amazon S3 with rclone. Documents remote configuration and a Vagrant / VirtualBox development environment for a basic cloud-storage workflow.

repositories.name: rclone-gdrive-project
repositories.title: File transfers to Google Drive
repositories.description: A small rclone transfer script and setup notes for copying files from a Linux virtual machine to Google Drive. An early automation exercise focused on remote configuration and command-line file transfer.

repositories.name: pydough-mcp-agent
repositories.title: PyDough MCP agent
repositories.description: Connects a Pydantic AI agent to a PyDough MCP server over stdio. Python opens the database session before the agent asks a question and requests closure, demonstrating an end-to-end tool workflow against SQLite sample data.

repositories.name: Collab_website
repositories.title: OpenTeams Collab release site
repositories.description: An interactive release-notes website for OpenTeams Collab. Built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with accessible navigation, feature switching, responsive layouts, and motion controls; included as supporting frontend engineering work.

repositories.name: Convex-Hull-using-Divide-and-Conquer
repositories.title: Convex hull: divide and conquer
repositories.description: Python implementation of a convex-hull algorithm using divide and conquer, brute-force handling for small inputs, and upper/lower tangent merging. Includes runtime measurements and a project report exploring the algorithm.

repositories.name: project1-runtime-analysis
repositories.title: Experimental runtime analysis
repositories.description: Measures an algorithm’s runtime across increasing input sizes and repeated trials, then reports average execution times. A Python exercise connecting empirical performance measurements with theoretical complexity analysis.

repositories.name: Vaidehi2510.github.io
repositories.title: Security engineering portfolio
repositories.description: The source for this security engineering portfolio: a responsive static site with searchable public projects, technical case studies, keyboard navigation, dark mode, and reduced-motion support. Published through GitHub Pages.

repositories.name: apollo-capabilities
repositories.title: Apollo capabilities
repositories.description: A public fork of OpenTeams’ catalog of standalone Pixi applications distributed as OCI artifacts. My open upstream PR proposes a PyDough MCP capability with a separate Python environment, a pinned dependency, and a default loopback bind.

contributions.summary: Proposed a standalone, locally bound PyDough MCP capability with an isolated dependency environment.

repositories.name: pydough-ce
repositories.title: PyDough Community Edition
repositories.description: A public fork of PyDough Community Edition for declarative analytics and SQL execution. My open upstream PR proposes fixes for SQLite paths, caller-selected database connections, and protecting caller-owned metadata during MCP session cleanup.

contributions.summary: Proposed upstream fixes to preserve the selected database connection and protect caller-owned metadata during MCP session cleanup.

repositories.name: frame-spec
repositories.title: Frame specification
repositories.description: A public fork of OpenTeams’ draft specification for text-based AI context. My merged contributions cover trusted-source guidance, sensitive-data handling, validator scope, and aligning required fields with the specification.

contributions.summary: Merged guidance on trusted sources, provenance limits, and inheritance behavior for AI context files.
Merged sensitive-data handling guidance for sharing organizational context with external AI services.
Documented validator scope so a frontmatter check is not mistaken for runtime or security assurance.
Aligned Frame validator required fields with the current specification.
